about.title: Tracy Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: When you go in for care in Tracy, you expect the people treating you to follow accepted standards. But when a diagnosis is missed, a medication is mixed up, or a surgical step goes wrong, the fallout lands on you and your family — often on top of the bills and the commute you were already juggling along I-205. Medical malpractice claims in San Joaquin County are governed by a California law called MICRA, and it works differently from an ordinary injury case. Deadlines are short: generally one year from the date you discovered the harm, and never more than three years from when it happened. A 90-day notice must be sent before a lawsuit can be filed. A qualified medical expert almost always has to review your records and confirm that the care fell below the standard, because a bad result by itself is not malpractice. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Tracy residents with an independent attorney who works on contingency — no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Tracy Patients Turn to LawProactive

items.title: MICRA's clock is shorter than most people think
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from discovering the injury, and no more than three years from when it occurred, to act. An attorney in our network can sort out which date applies to you before the window closes.

items.title: The 90-day notice and expert review are handled early
items.desc: Before a malpractice suit can be filed in San Joaquin County, a 90-day notice of intent must go out and a qualified medical expert nearly always needs to weigh in. The attorneys we connect you with build these steps into the case from day one.

items.title: Honest assessment, including the cap on non-economic damages
items.desc: MICRA limits non-economic damages, though that cap rises each year under current law. You'll get a clear explanation of what that means for your situation — not a sales pitch.

items.question: I live in Tracy but was treated in Stockton or the Bay Area. Can LawProactive still help?
items.answer: Yes. Many Tracy residents receive care outside the city, and where the treatment happened does not prevent you from getting connected. The attorney you're matched with will look at where the care occurred and where you live to decide the proper court for any filing. Your first conversation is free either way.

items.question: My surgery didn't turn out the way I hoped. Is that automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law is clear that a poor outcome on its own is not malpractice. What matters is whether the provider's care fell below what a reasonably careful provider would have done in the same situation, and whether that failure caused your injury. A qualified medical expert almost always has to review the records to answer that question.

items.question: How much does it cost to have a Tracy malpractice attorney look at my case?
items.answer: Nothing up front. LawProactive is a free connection service, and the independent attorneys in our network take medical malpractice cases on contingency. That means their fee comes only out of a recovery, and if there is no recovery, you owe no attorney fee.
